findings.title: hastub Store decodes with stdlib json: 6 of 6 hostile number tokens load where HA's orjson Store drops the file
findings.claim: For 6 stored documents holding one healthy leaf and one hostile number token (NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, 1e400, a 401-digit integer, 2**64), QuarantiningStore.async_load over tests/hastub's Store returns a different payload than over Home Assistant's orjson codec in 6 of 6: the stub keeps the healthy sibling in all 6 where Home Assistant loses the whole store in 5, and the stub hands a 401-digit exact int to the loader that Home Assistant never produces.
findings.mechanism: tests/hastub/homeassistant/helpers/storage.py round-trips through stdlib json, which accepts NaN/Infinity tokens, decodes 1e400 as inf and keeps arbitrary-precision ints. Home Assistant's Store reads with orjson, which refuses those tokens (and >64-bit literals past double range), logs 'Unrecoverable error decoding storage', moves the file aside and returns None. So every store-fuzz verdict through the stub is leaf-level where Home Assistant's is whole-store: the stub-only raises D1-s1 and D1-s2 reported (19 of 250 accuracy mutants; energy and defrost 10**400) come from it, and the whole-store reset a corrupt file causes in Home Assistant is invisible to the suite.

findings.metric_definition: Hostile stored documents (of 6) whose QuarantiningStore.async_load payload through the stub differs from the payload through Home Assistant's orjson decode-or-None.
findings.phenomenon_property: The test double for Home Assistant's Store decodes and encodes exactly as Home Assistant's does (orjson; a document it cannot decode loads as None), so a store fuzz through it reports what Home Assistant would do.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: tests/hastub storage.Store: decode with orjson when importable (it is a Home Assistant core dependency) and return None on a decode error; encode NaN as null as orjson does. Re-run tests/finite_boundary.py and the store fuzzers.

findings.title: hastub dt_util.now() is naive by default: the naive-vs-aware verdict of 6 of 6 stored-timestamp cells is inverted
findings.claim: On the stub's default clock (no HASTUB_TZ, not frozen aware), dt_util.now() is naive, so for D1-s1-01's three seams (SnapshotRing.due, CurveLearner._step_down, ComfortLearner._decay) an aware stored stamp raises TypeError in 3 of 3 and a naive one in 0 of 3 -- the opposite of Home Assistant, where now is always aware -- 6 of 6 cells divergent.
findings.mechanism: tests/hastub/homeassistant/util/dt.py:now returns datetime.now() unless HASTUB_TZ is set or freeze() was given an aware instant. A test on that clock never meets the naive-stored failure production meets (D1-s1-01, D1-s3-01 and D14-s1-01 are its instances) and would see the healthy aware case fail, so such tests either freeze naive or avoid the comparison; store_fuzz.py --naive-clock (D1-s3) lost every naive_dt failure for this reason.

findings.title: A learner or arbiter raise on the cycle path fails the solve or the whole cycle and skips actuation and saves
findings.claim: A raise inside ComfortLearner.record_quiet_period makes async_run_optimization return 'solve_failed' with an ERROR traceback on 3 of 3 cycles although the plan was published, and a raise inside pump_arbiter.apply makes _async_update_data fail 3 of 3 cycles and skip 15 of 15 sibling steps (frequency command, pump drive, accuracy and energy saves, drift watch).
findings.mechanism: _record_quiet_comfort_period is called unfenced inside async_run_optimization's try after _optimization_result and _solve_failures=0 are set, so its raise lands in the solve's except (logged 'Optimization failed', counter set to 1 each cycle, _command_valve_target skipped). pump_arbiter.apply is awaited unfenced as the first line of _apply_action, while its siblings _command_frequency, _async_drive_pumps and _async_watch_learning_drift are each fenced; an arbiter raise therefore aborts the cycle before them and before _async_save_accuracy/_async_save_energy_totals. D1-s3-03 (non-numeric pump_duty set-point) and D1-s3-01 (naive stored timestamp in hold()) are real producers of such a raise.

findings.title: Five store writers do not wait for the startup read: a save in that window replaces persisted learned state
findings.claim: When a store's writer runs while its startup load (spawned fire-and-forget in the coordinator's __init__) is still in flight, the restarted coordinator ends with the defaults instead of the persisted state in 5 of 5 stores (energy totals 1234.5 -> 0.0, ledger operation score 77 -> None, house heat-loss scale 1.3 -> 1.0, price-model days seen 2 -> 0, comfort weight 7.5 -> 5.0), while async_set_mode, the one writer that awaits async_wait_for_read, loses nothing.
findings.mechanism: R6's startup-clobber fix added QuarantiningStore.async_wait_for_read and put it in async_set_mode only. _async_save_energy_totals, _async_save_ledger, _async_save_thermal_learning, _async_save_price_model and _async_save_accuracy (called from the cycle end, async_reset_comfort_weight, sysid adoption, the settlement path) save their whole in-memory payload without waiting, so a save that precedes the read replaces the file (or, in Home Assistant, is the pending data the read returns) and the loader then installs the defaults. The energy loader's max() guard does not help: it reads the clobbered value.

findings.title: set_thermal_parameters changes are silently lost at the next restart (24 of 26 fields)
findings.claim: Of the 26 set_thermal_parameters fields whose call changes coordinator state, 24 revert to the configured value after a Home Assistant restart on the same entry and store disk; only dhw_cooling_rate and buffer_cooling_rate, which the thermal-learning store carries, survive.
findings.mechanism: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_update_thermal_params assigns the fields onto the live _thermal_params/_opt_config (the _THERMAL_PARAM_FIELDS table and the explicit branches) and persists only the learned cooling rates via _async_save_thermal_learning. Nothing writes the other fields to entry.options or a store, and a restart rebuilds ThermalParameters/OptimizationConfig from the entry, so the service's effect lasts until the next restart with no log line, repair or doc sentence saying so (configuration.md:924 says only that it 'writes model parameters at runtime').

findings.title: apply_manual_plan accepts expires_at past the horizon: the override owns all 96 steps, the invariant it states is unenforced
findings.claim: With space_slots=[] and expires_at=now+48h, handle_apply_manual_plan installs an override whose channel_pins leave 0 of 96 horizon steps free at apply time and 0 of 96 twenty-three hours later, against 16 and 96 with the default expiry, although const.MANUAL_PLAN_WINDOW_HOURS documents 'override shorter than horizon' as the invariant that stops a daily re-apply switching the optimizer off while appearing to leave it on.
findings.mechanism: handle_apply_manual_plan uses MANUAL_PLAN_WINDOW_HOURS only as the default; an explicit expires_at is parsed and passed to build_override, which refuses only a past expiry. Nothing caps it at now + MANUAL_PLAN_WINDOW_HOURS (or below the horizon), so the override pins every step and the optimizer plans nothing on that channel.

findings.title: A solve worker that cannot start (Popen OSError) skips the in-process fallback: no plan, no fallback notice
findings.claim: With subprocess.Popen raising OSError(EAGAIN) when the solve worker is spawned, 0 of 3 cycles publish a plan and no solve_worker_fallback notice is raised, while the same failure re-raised as ProcessWorkerUnavailable yields 3 of 3 plans through the in-process fallback and the notice.
findings.mechanism: _run_in_process calls _ensure_worker() (subprocess.Popen) inside _PROCESS_LOCK but before its try, so a spawn OSError escapes as OSError. _await_optimize catches only ProcessWorkerUnavailable, so the #511 degrade (in-process solve, _note_worker_fallback) is skipped and the OSError lands in async_run_optimization's generic except as 'Optimization failed'.

findings.title: A report-on-change indoor thermometer silent over 60 min turns Indoor Temperature unavailable while HA holds its valid reading
findings.claim: With the indoor thermometer's state '21.3' valid in Home Assistant but last reported 61, 90, 240 or 480 min ago, the integration's Indoor Temperature sensor is unavailable in 4 of 7 silence cells (available at 5-59 min), and a thermometer that re-writes an unchanged value (last_reported 5 min, last_updated 480 min) stays available, so the gaps come from genuine report silence, not from ignoring last_reported.
findings.mechanism: InputReader._age_gate marks the indoor reading stale once its last_reported/last_updated age exceeds INPUT_MAX_AGE_MINUTES[indoor] = 60 min (x staleness scale, default 1.0); reading_ok['upper_floor_temperature'] goes False and _MeasuredTemperatureMixin.available follows it. A thermometer that reports only on change (common for battery Zigbee/BLE sensors: a stable room for hours sends nothing and Home Assistant writes nothing) therefore reads as dead, contradicting const.py's stated intent that the limits are 'generous multiples of a normal reporting interval so that a healthy sensor never trips them'. The user sees history gaps (reported: ~16:30-20:45 and ~03:30-06:15 local, the stable hours); the same stale flag also withholds the reading from the cycle. D1-s5-01's age_of seam (inlet/humidity) ignores last_reported, but this path does not: its re-report arm is available.

evidence.unit: silence cells with Indoor Temperature unavailable while the source state is valid

findings.phenomenon_property: A measured input whose source entity still holds a valid state in Home Assistant is not published as unavailable merely because a healthy report-on-change device sent nothing for an hour; staleness of such inputs is judged by the source's own availability or a limit its reporting pattern cannot trip. Too-eager question (orchestrator addendum): the guard is too eager exactly for report-on-change thermometers silent over 60 min (4 of 7 cells, every silence >= 61 min); an unchanged value that moves only last_reported does NOT trip it (rereport_unavailable=0 of 1). How often real devices exceed 60 min was not measurable in this container (no device report-interval corpus); the field evidence is the reported gaps in the stable hours (~16:30-20:45, ~03:30-06:15 local).

findings.title: DHW setpoint advisor prices candidates at the 5.0 degC ThermalState default when no outdoor thermometer is mapped
findings.claim: On a hot-water install without an outdoor thermometer, _dhw_setpoint_sweep prices all 7 candidates at outdoor 5.0 degC (the constructor default) instead of the forecast the plan uses, so the published cost_per_day is off by more than 5 % on 7 of 7 candidates at a -15 degC forecast (worst 52.7 %) and at -5 degC (worst 26.5 %); the recommended setpoint is unchanged.
findings.mechanism: _dhw_setpoint_sweep reads float(ctx._current_state.outdoor_temperature), which _update_current_state only overwrites from an ok outdoor-thermometer reading; without one it stays ThermalState's 5.0 default, and compute_cop_dhw(5.0, t) overstates the COP. forecast_outdoor_now and sensor._effective_outdoor exist for exactly this case and the outdoor sensor already uses them.

findings.title: nightly_ha._async_check_a4 returns inside finally: an in-flight CancelledError or KeyboardInterrupt is swallowed
findings.claim: When the broken-price refresh raises a BaseException the inner handler does not catch (CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt) and the recovery refresh then raises, tests/nightly_ha.py:_async_check_a4 returns normally in 2 of 2 arms because of the `return` inside its finally (tests/nightly_ha.py:1274), and CPython 3.14 emits 1 SyntaxWarning compiling the file (PEP 765).
findings.mechanism: The recovery block in the outer finally catches Exception from the second async_refresh and returns; a return in finally discards any exception propagating from the try, so a cancellation or interrupt that reached the finally (a lane timeout, a runner stop) ends the A4 check as an ordinary recorded failure instead of stopping the run.
